name: Illusion Crafting
reason: Term coined for the adaptation to name the source's practice of refining weapons with illusion effects (the ch. 22 Scarlet Fantasy Gravel passage); the source has no single name for this craft.
description: The craft of forging weapons that carry illusion effects. Mentioned in Ep 38 when Zane recognizes a blood-red ore as an essential material for Illusion Crafting, mirroring the source's Scarlet Fantasy Gravel, which grants refined weapons an illusion effect.

name: Finn's Extreme Thunder Sword Intent
reason: Possessive surface form of the technique 'Extreme Thunder Sword Intent'; the source uses the identical English term for Hua Tianming's (Finn's) sword intent.
description: Finn's evolved sword technique combining the Celestial Blade with the power of thunder, mastered after the Sword Tempering Pool (Eps 305-307); matches Hua Tianming's Extreme Thunder Sword Intent in the source.

name: Proving Ground
reason: Adaptation name for a sparring arena in the Cloud Hall arc; no specific source location was identified for it.
description: An enclosed training and dueling arena with heavy doors used during the Cloud Hall arc; Zane used his Corrupt Vitality there to swallow Richard's Hymn of Justice in front of Finn and Patrick.

name: Drake's Blood
reason: The source's 'Flood Dragon's Blood' (the Flood Dragon's Blood Pool, ch. 384) was localized as 'Drake's Blood', using 'drake' for the flood dragon, a lesser dragon.
description: A pool of viscous drake (flood dragon) blood found in Vesper's tomb, its name carved on the wall in flowing script (Ep 397). Bathing in it cleanses and strengthens the body with pure draconic energy, and the blood is precious even to a Sixth-Grade Sect.

name: Heavenly Fruit Tree
reason: The source's clunky 'Heaven End Dao Fruit Tree' (ch. 397, aligned with Ep 397, which is even titled 'Heavenly Fruit Tree') was simplified to 'Heavenly Fruit Tree' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A legendary tree encountered in the Vesper's-tomb arc around Eps 397-410; its fruit is a coveted treasure tied to the trials there.

name: Master Isla
reason: Title-plus-name surface form of Isla Novak, the Sky Princess and sect mentor (source Su Lingyun/Mentor Su); 'Master' is her mentor title at the sect.
description: Isla Novak in her capacity as a sect master/mentor: in Ep 40 she rules on a disturbance and then quietly covers for the irregularity in Zane's Student ID, mirroring Su Lingyun shielding Luo Zheng in the source.

name: Restless Mind
reason: The source's garbled rendering of the fifth sign of an immortal's decay ('not happy this seat', ch. 388) was localized as 'Restless Mind' to make the Five Signs of Decay intelligible.
description: The fifth and final sign of a celestial being's decay, after Filthy Clothing, Falling Hair, Sweating Armpits and a Stinky Body (Ep 401). Once a celestial reaches the Restless Mind, their immortality shatters and they die like any mortal, as the celestial Vesper did after returning to his homeland.

name: Vitality-based
reason: Adjectival fragment ('Vitality-based messaging rune', 'Vitality-based cultivation'), not a standalone entity.

name: Cloud Hall Zane
reason: Sentence-boundary concatenation of 'Cloud Hall' and 'Zane', not an entity; both components are covered by their own entries.

name: Lion-mane Ape
reason: The source beast 'Maned Demon Monkey' (a Level Two Phantom Beast, ch. ~25) was localized as 'Lion-mane Ape' for a more vivid Western creature name.
description: A shrieking maned primate beast Zane fights on Bloody Mountain during The Gauntlet (Ep 41); corresponds to the Level Two Phantom Beast Maned Demon Monkey of the source's Trial of Blood.

name: Fusion Realm
reason: The source's own English term 'Fusion Realm'/'Fusion Stage' for the legendary pinnacle of puppetry (ch. 401) was kept as-is.
description: Not a cultivation stage but the legendary peak of puppetry mastery: a puppet master at the Fusion Realm can channel his own power directly into his marionette, as Saint Morphen (source Daoist Dameng) does when puppeting fighters against Zane (Eps 414, 459).

name: Ancient Phoenix
reason: The source's 'Ancient Phoenix Clan' of the Upper Realm was carried over nearly verbatim, dropping 'Clan' in this mention.
description: An ancient phoenix lineage of the Upper Realm, referenced around Ep 418; even the Cobalt Dragon cannot read the writing of the Ancient Phoenix Clan in the source.

name: Ancient Phoenix Language
original_name: words of the ancient phoenix clan
reason: The source's 'words of the Ancient Phoenix Clan' was tightened into the term 'Ancient Phoenix Language'.
description: The script of the Ancient Phoenix Clan of the Upper Realm (Ep 419), an ancient writing so obscure that not even the Cobalt Dragon can read it.

name: Frost-Leaf Herb
reason: Adaptation-coined herb name in the Western fantasy register; no specific source herb was identified as its counterpart.
description: A rare herb Randy found on the Death Road (Ep 385); its roots require special handling in refinement and it serves as a minor ingredient alongside Potent Azurewood Root (Eps 419-420).

name: Dragon's Tooth Peak
reason: Western-fantasy name given to one of the Skyreach Sect's peaks; the specific source peak it maps to (the Blue Cloud Sect has peaks such as Vulture Peak and Little Rain Peak) was not identified.
description: One of the Skyreach Sect's peaks, presided over by mentor Chris Fane of House Fane (Eps 42-45); Joe, the Gauntlet's strongest candidate, was all but guaranteed to join it through his relative Master Fane.

name: Joe's Student ID
reason: Possessive common-noun phrase; the Student ID item and the character Joe are covered by their own entries.

name: Lady Tia
reason: Honorific surface form of Tia, the Cloud Hall disciple revealed as a powerful woman (Ep 390); she matches source Xiao Die ('Little Butterfly'), the disguised female disciple seeking the Sixth-Grade Sect's crystal and wielding an Ice Phoenix.

name: Tier-Three
reason: Adjectival grading fragment ('eight Tier-Three sects'), not a standalone entity.

name: Innate Realm
issues: Possible name drift: the episodes' canonical rendering of source Xiantian/Connate appears to be 'Nature Level' (cf. the Life Energy/Life Force canon rule), while 'Innate Realm' surfaces only in Eps 428 and 1017 for the same stage.
reason: Renders the source cultivation stage 'Xiantian' (innate/connate), the threshold at which Genuine Qi transforms into Natal Vital Essence.
description: A rendering of the Xiantian (innate) cultivation stage, used when Nash sizes up Zane's cultivation (Ep 428) and in Ep 1017's recollection of Zane 'barely past the Innate Realm'; elsewhere the show calls this stage the Nature Level.

name: Zane’s Dragon Scales
reason: Possessive descriptive phrase for the Cobalt Dragon's scales manifesting on Zane's body, not a standalone entity.

name: Kendrick
reason: The source's Xue Family, the clan whose young lord contests the Rising Dragon Arena (ch. ~421), was localized as the Western-style 'House Kendrick'.
description: A noble house long rumored to carry dragon's blood (Eps 432-434). Its young master, a late-stage Inner-Core warrior, held the Dragon Crystal Pendant that opens the Dragon Soar Arena and raced Zane to its sixth floor.

name: Cerulean City
reason: Adaptation-coined city name in the Dragon Soar Arena region; no named source city was identified at the aligned chapters.
description: A city near where Zane emerges during the Dragon Soar Arena arc (Eps 434-435); its guards seize him as a trespasser and haul him inside.

name: Obelisks of Souls
reason: The source's law-recording 'obelisks' (ch. 425) were given the fuller title 'Obelisks of Souls' for the adaptation.
description: Towering obelisks that each hold the complete power of an Original Law, such as Fire or Space (Ep 437); meditating on them lets a cultivator comprehend those Laws far faster, an opportunity rare enough that some stay for years.

name: Lower World Christopher
reason: Sentence-boundary concatenation of 'Lower World' and the character Christopher, not an entity.

name: Wraithblades
reason: The source weapon pair 'War Ghost Dual Blades' (ch. 431, aligned with Ep 444) was condensed into the punchier 'Wraithblades'.
description: A paired set of ghost-themed blades revealed with a shout in Ep 444 during the Rising Dragon/War Soul arc; corresponds to the source's War Ghost Dual Blades.

name: Dragon’s Heartblood
reason: The source's 'True Dragon's Blood' (chs. 436-444), sold by the drop to densify dragon bloodlines, was localized as 'True Dragon's Heartblood'; this dossier form is the shortened mid-sentence mention.
description: An extraordinarily precious substance offered by the drop; a single drop can thicken a warrior's dragon bloodline. Madame Vermillion's offer of a drop to Zane (Ep 450) signaled his untouchable status during the nine True Dragons affair.

name: Runic Circles
reason: Adaptation term for the containment formations sealing beasts on Bloody Mountain during The Gauntlet; no named source counterpart was identified.
description: Containment formations on Bloody Mountain that confine the trial's beasts to their assigned levels; in Ep 47 an Ogre inexplicably breaks through the Runic Circles from the fifth level down to the third, throwing The Gauntlet into crisis.

name: Master Corrin
reason: The character appears to be an adaptation-named figure for the unnamed drill-yard trainer of the source's opening chapters; 'Corrin' was chosen as a plain, period-fitting name for a minor functionary.
description: The sadistic trainer who runs the Lowell family drill yard where slaves serve as living punching bags for the clan's children (Eps 5-9); he is quick to use his skin-flaying whip on any slave who flinches.

name: Close Quarters Combat
reason: Generic capitalized phrase for melee fighting, not a named entity.

name: Seven Ruling Houses
reason: The source's 'Seven Great Families' (the seven great noble families whose reputation resounds through the empire) was localized as 'Seven Ruling Houses' to match the show's 'House' nomenclature.
description: The seven most powerful noble houses of the Empire, House Sterling among them (Ep 55); their scions enjoy enormous privilege, standing above even wealthy landowning houses.

name: Thunderstrike
reason: Adaptation-named technique for Tristan's lightning attack in the Ep 56 duel; no specific source technique was identified as its counterpart.
description: A powerful lightning technique described as an upgrade path, used by Tristan against Zane in Ep 56; Zane met it head-on with the Shadow Fist from his Purple Flash Fist technique.

name: Mystic Weapons
issues: Superseded variant: Eps 70 and 99 use 'Mystic Weapon(s)' for the tier-3 weapon class, but the show's canon decision makes 'Mythic Weapon' canonical (the 'Mystic' policy was reversed for Eps 451+).
reason: Plural of the early 'Mystic Weapon' rendering of the source's tier-3 Xuan Weapon class; folds into the canonical 'Mythic Weapon'.

name: Dragon’s Keep
reason: The source location 'Dragon Castle' (chs. 48-175, aligned with this arc) was localized as 'Dragon's Keep' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A stronghold from which the cold, calculating Nature Level fighter Randall hails (Ep 72); corresponds to the source's Dragon Castle in the Blade Insect arc.

name: General Gavin
reason: 'Gavin' was chosen as a rugged soldierly name for this Empire powerhouse; per the master sheet the 'General' prefix is always used. No specific source counterpart was identified in the aligned chapters.
description: A renowned military powerhouse of the Empire (Eps 79, 87) who can cross hundreds of feet in a single step and openly scoffs at House Sterling; later fighters are measured against his level of lethality.

name: Gavin
issues: Split reference: the Ep 79 'Gavin' mentions are General Gavin, but Ep 1252's Gavin is a different character - Zane and Tia's seven-year-old son, left behind in the Lower World when Tia ascended. Do not merge the two under one entry.
reason: The bare name covers two distinct characters (General Gavin in Ep 79; Zane and Tia's young son in Ep 1252), so it is kept as its own row rather than aliased.
description: In Ep 79 the name refers to General Gavin; in Ep 1252 it names Zane and Tia's son, barely seven years old, whom Tia left behind in the Lower World when she broke through to the Soul Sea Realm and ascended to search for Zane.

name: Sacred Lunge
reason: Adaptation-named signature technique for Seth in the Ep 80 arena fight; no specific source technique was confidently identified as its counterpart.
description: Seth's signature attack, a series of deadly lunging strikes (Ep 80); Zane effortlessly weaves around it, making every strike miss by inches.

name: Aegis Band
reason: Likely a localization of the source's defensive 'Thick Earth Ring' from the aligned arena chapters (chs. 70-71), renamed 'Aegis Band' for its protective function; the match is plausible but not certain.
description: A defensive ring-type treasure that pulses with dormant energy, its surface rippling like liquid metal, seen in Finn's hand during the arena arc (Eps 82-83).

name: Council Robes
reason: Adaptation-coined name for the Skyreach Sect's elite-disciple robes (the source marks such elites by robe color, e.g. Wang Yanmiao's purple robes, without a named institution).
description: Deep-hued robes of the Skyreach Sect reserved for the select disciples personally mentored by the masters in Enhancement skills, marking elite status above the Pledges' White Robes and the Varsity's Shadow Cloaks (Eps 88-89); Adrian Warrick wears them.
